scenarios.title: Dead File Reference
scenarios.event: CLAUDE.md references src/old_module.ts but the file was deleted 5 commits ago.

scenarios.title: Broken Build Command
scenarios.event: CLAUDE.md says build with make test but the Makefile was replaced by package.json scripts.

scenarios.title: Undocumented New Files
scenarios.event: Three new files were added to src/api/ in recent commits. CLAUDE.md doesnt mention them.

scenarios.title: Config Drift — Missing Env Var
scenarios.event: CLAUDE.md references REDIS_URL but its not in .env.example.

scenarios.title: Stale Architecture Description
scenarios.event: CLAUDE.md says Entry: git-crypt.cpp → commands.cpp but commands.cpp was renamed to handler.cpp.

scenarios.title: Correct Severity Classification
scenarios.event: Dead file ref should be HIGH. Undocumented new file should be MEDIUM. Orphaned memory bank entry should be LOW.

scenarios.title: Respect .context-drift-ignore
scenarios.event: legacy/ directory is in .context-drift-ignore. CLAUDE.md references a deleted file in legacy/. Should be suppressed.

scenarios.title: Generate Fix Suggestions
scenarios.event: A HIGH severity dead file ref is found. Should generate a specific fix suggestion.

scenarios.title: Use Git History for Context
scenarios.event: Instructions should guide using git log --name-status to understand what changed.

scenarios.title: Integration with context-loader
scenarios.event: After drift fixes, context-loader should refresh ecosystem context. Instructions should mention this.

criteria: Detection Coverage: Do instructions cover all drift types (dead refs, broken commands, stale arch)?
Severity Classification: Do instructions correctly guide HIGH vs MEDIUM vs LOW severity?
Git Integration: Do instructions guide using git history for change context?
Ignore File: Do instructions support .context-drift-ignore for suppressing known drift?
Fix Generation: Do instructions guide producing specific fix suggestions for HIGH issues?
Skill Integration: Do instructions reference context-loader as a follow-up action?
